title: Tanzanian Lentil Curry
community: Popular across Tanzania — particularly among South Asian-influenced communities
author: Chef Fatuma
desc: Tanzanian Dengu — red or green lentils simmered in a fragrant Zanzibar spice and tomato sauce until completely soft and creamy. Fast, affordable, and intensely nutritious — the lentil curry that reflects Tanzania's Indian Ocean culinary exchange.
longDesc: Dengu is one of Tanzania's most popular legume dishes — lentils cook far faster than dried beans, require no soaking, and absorb spices beautifully. The Indian Ocean spice influence is clearly felt in the Zanzibar-influenced spicing.
steps: Heat oil. Cook onions until golden.
Add garlic, ginger, and all spices. Stir 1 minute.
Add tomatoes. Cook 6 minutes until thick.
Simmer uncovered for 20—25 minutes until lentils are completely soft and the mixture is creamy.
Add lemon juice. Garnish with coriander.
chefTips: Red lentils need no soaking — very fast to cook.
Stir occasionally — lentils can stick to the bottom.
The lentils should completely dissolve into a creamy consistency.
commonMistakes: Under-cooking — lentils should be completely soft.
cookingScience: Red lentils have had their outer seed coat removed — they cook in 20 minutes without soaking because the water can penetrate immediately. They also contain more soluble starch than whole lentils, which dissolves during cooking to produce the characteristic creamy consistency.
sustainabilityTips: Lentils are nitrogen-fixing like beans — very sustainable protein.
reheating: Gently with a splash of water.
culturalNote: Dengu reflects Tanzania's Indian Ocean food heritage — lentils arrived on the coast through centuries of trade with the Indian subcontinent and have been completely absorbed into Tanzanian cooking.
